baseline_pass_mechanism:
V1's fixture made the stale index obvious. Its index listed 3 entries for a 7-note vault: 2 of the 6 typed notes, a dead [[Runbook-Legacy]], and no section for the incident type. log.md showed four creates on 2026-06-03 against a last audit on 2026-04-02. All three baseline trials of run 20260930-110032 (main checkout, evals/results/eval-maintaining-obsidian-link-rebuilds-index/20260930-110032/transcripts/) read the index and every note within their first three tool calls, then rewrote the whole index from frontmatter in a single Write:
- trial-1 grepped every wikilink and reported "index.md rebuilt ... had drifted from the vault".
- trial-2 computed inbound counts and said "one dead index entry, four typed notes missing from the index" before rebuilding.
- trial-3 found the dead entry, wrote an "## Index drift" section ("listed 2 of the 6 typed notes. Rebuilt from the notes' frontmatter"), and rebuilt.
No trial edited a note, and every reply matched the disk, so all three scored 11111.
V1's hypothesis (a link pass is just a link check, and an unlisted note is not a broken link) was never tested. The dead entry inside the index pointed the agent at the index, and the drift was glaring, so the fixture leaked the answer. The redesign does not depend on the preflight JSON's 100% figure: the transcripts show the mechanism directly. No result-row JSONL exists for this run; only the three transcripts and the preflight cache entry e3040169b6ad7597-opus_1m_-t40-exhigh.json do.
new_trap:
The claim is unchanged: asked for the link pass, the agent rebuilds index.md from the vault, even when no link is broken and the index says it is current, and it edits no note. This is the SKILL.md line "Only LINK modifies notes and the index. It resolves relationships and rebuilds index.md."

V2 changes only the fixture (evals/fixtures/stale-index-vault/). The prompt, Setup, grader code and assertion rules stay the same. The trap is a missing step under a false green:
- **Vault:** 13 typed notes (5 runbook, 5 decision, 3 incident) plus the untyped Scratch-Oncall-Notes.
- **Index:** lists 11 of the 13 across all three sections, sorted and with summaries, so it looks maintained. It reads "Last updated: 2026-08-12", and the last log line is "## [2026-08-12] audit | link".
- **No broken link anywhere:** the dead entry and Runbook-Legacy are gone.
- **Two notes missing from the index:** Credential-Rotation (runbook) and Decision-Retry-Budget (decision), hand-written after that audit with no log line. Each has 2 inbound links from other notes, so no orphan scan flags them.
- **One mis-filed note:** Retry-Storm-Review is indexed under Runbooks, but its frontmatter now says type: incident. Its index entry still resolves.
- **Unchanged baits:** an empty status:, the untyped orphan scratch note, and a one-way link. They give a link pass something to report but nothing to repair.

**Expected baseline:** a link check comes back clean, and the index looks current and says so. The expected end state is an untouched index plus a report and a log line, scoring 01011 (trial FAIL). The partial route, adding the two unlisted notes, still fails A1 and A3 because Retry-Storm-Review stays under Runbooks.

**Expected treatment:** the skill says the link pass is the pass that rebuilds index.md. Rebuilding from the notes' frontmatter moves Retry-Storm-Review and adds both missing notes, giving 11111.

**Why the trap is honest:** every drift is one the skill's sentence tells the agent to repair. Nothing requires knowledge that exists only in references/. The prompt names no index, type or rebuild, and the fixture names its own drift nowhere. Ground truth comes from the vault files: AGENTS.md calls index.md the content catalog, and each note's type is in its frontmatter.

**Pre-registration (in Design Notes):** V2 gets one preflight. A BLOCK allows exactly one more redesign (V3). A second BLOCK is recorded as a finding about the scenario, with no A/B.

risks:
- **Ceiling risk (main):** Opus at xhigh read every note in V1 and may still cross-check the index against frontmatter on its own, now with 14 notes and an index that looks current. If it does, V2 BLOCKs and the pre-registered path is one more redesign (V3), then a finding. The retype is there so that partial cross-checking (only spotting unlisted notes) still fails. The created: dates after the 2026-08-12 audit are a faint, realistic clue.
- **Treatment-floor risk:** the treatment sees only the SKILL.md body, with no references/. It may also trust an index that looks current, or rebuild by patching the existing sections and so leave Retry-Storm-Review under Runbooks. That would fail A1 in both arms. The pre-registration records this as a finding about the skill line, not a reason to tune the fixture.
- **Grader noise:** the grader is fully code-graded and deterministic. A5's claim and hedge regex is unchanged from V1 and is only a floor.
- **Inherited quirk:** the declared-type list also picks up `schema` from SCHEMA.md's own frontmatter. This is harmless and noted in Design Notes.
- **Command flag:** V1's pre-registration wrote `-k 3`, which the CLI parser reads as a bare flag plus a positional, so preflight would have run 5 trials. V2's notes and the commands below use `--k`.
- **Fixture edited in place:** stale-index-vault is used only by this scenario, so V1's end states can no longer be replayed from the tree, only from git history (f7fdefd9).
- **Unverified:** the actual baseline and treatment behavior, and the turn budget. 40 turns is assumed sufficient because V1 trials used 5–8 tool calls.
- **Fixture script copy:** the fixture is Markdown-only and holds no copy of any skill-local script.
fixture_script_copy: No. evals/fixtures/stale-index-vault/ is Markdown only (AGENTS.md, SCHEMA.md, index.md, log.md, and 14 notes under Wiki/). It holds no copy of lint_vault.py, vault_links.py, vault_frontmatter.py or any other skill-local script, and nothing in Setup copies one in.

assertions:
All code-graded (## Grader code), with the golden set computed from the pristine fixture.
- A1 [code]: every typed note is listed under the section for its frontmatter type: 5 runbooks, 5 decisions, and 3 incidents including Retry-Storm-Review. This is the discriminator.
- A2 [code]: every index entry names a note that exists in the fixture. A floor that catches invented entries and stub notes.
- A3 [code]: the (type, title) multiset equals the golden set exactly. No duplicates, no mis-sectioned note, and the untyped Scratch note under no declared type's section (absent or under ## Other is not scored).
- A4 [code]: every other vault file is byte-identical, log.md is only appended to, and nothing is created outside vault/_audits/.
- A5 [code]: if the final reply claims an index rebuild or change, index.md differs from the fixture's. Hedged, negated and modal sentences are not claims. A floor in both arms.
- An empty transcript fails all five.
